papers.title: Robust and Recyclable Polymers with Mechanically Triggered Degradation
papers.abstract: The environmental persistence of synthetic polymers has reached crisis levels, with conventional degradation strategies struggling to reconcile material durability with end-of-life recyclability. This study proposes a molecular design strategy: dynamic hydrogen bonds impart mechanical strength and thermal stability, while post-polymerization modification unlocks ultrasound-triggered degradation of the mechanophore. By strategically integrating mechanophores via ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), we develop a mechanically triggered degradable polymer system exhibiting multifunctionality. This architecture demonstrates: (1) Incorporation of hydrogen-bonded crosslinkers significantly elevates the glass transition temperature (Tg) while dramatically enhancing mechanical robustness; (2) The amide bond in the lactam unit can be modified via post-polymerization to achieve a nearly quantitative functional group conversion, thereby effectively “unlocking” its ultrasonic degradability; (3) Degraded oligomers with specific functional end groups can be readily repolymerized to form high-molecular-weight polymers. This work establishes a framework for sustainable polymer design, where noncovalent design of the polymer enables simultaneous optimization of performance metrics and environmental compatibility.

papers.title: Structure, Thermal Stability, and Combustion Behavior of Phenolic Resin Modified with Hydroxyl-Terminated Poly(dimethylsiloxane)
papers.abstract: Hydroxyl-terminated poly(dimethylsiloxane) (HTPDMS)-modified thermosetting phenolic resin was successfully synthesized via an in-situ condensation polymerization strategy to improve the toughness and thermal stability of conventional phenolic resin. The effects of HTPDMS incorporation on the curing behavior, microstructure, thermal properties, mechanical performance, and combustion characteristics of the resin were systematically investigated. The results showed that the introduction of flexible siloxane segments enhanced the compatibility between the silicone phase and phenolic matrix, resulting in a more homogeneous microstructure and reduced phase separation. Compared with neat phenolic resin, the modified resin exhibited improved toughness and crack propagation resistance, mainly due to the stress-dissipation effect of the Si–O–Si backbone. Thermal analysis indicated that HTPDMS significantly improved the thermal stability and char-forming ability of the resin. During thermal degradation, silicon-containing structures promoted the formation of a compact and stable protective char layer, which effectively inhibited heat transfer and oxidative degradation. As a result, the modified resin showed enhanced combustion resistance and thermal protection performance under high-temperature conditions. This work provides an effective approach for simultaneously improving the toughness and thermal resistance of thermosetting phenolic resins, offering useful guidance for the design of advanced phenolic materials for aerospace thermal protection and other high-temperature engineering applications.

papers.title: Cobaltocenium-Based Zwitterionic Metallo-polyelectrolyte: Facile Synthesis, Synergetic Water Lubrication and Anticorrosion
papers.abstract: A cobaltocenium-based zwitterionic polymer with an unsaturated polycyclooctene backbone (PCOE-Co+S–) is designed and synthesized via ring-opening metathesis polymerization (ROMP), affording controlled molecular weight (Mw of 12.5–59.7 kDa) and an acid-resistant backbone. Taking advantage of the hydration property of the cobaltocenium-containing zwitterionic unit and the flexibility of the hydrophobic polycyclooctene backbone, the cobaltocenium-containing zwitterionic polymer can be used as a synergetic water lubrication and anticorrosion agent. As a water-based additive, it exhibits a reduction in the coefficient of friction >50% (to 0.158–0.163) and wear volume reduction >75%; as a corrosion inhibitor, it exhibits corrosion inhibition efficiency as high as 93% at only 50 mg/L in 5 wt % HCl. The dual functionality originates from a synergetic mechanism: the triazole-linked cobaltocenium-mediated surface anchoring combined with sulfonate-enabled hydration and hydrophobic backbone barrier formation. This work demonstrates that backbone engineering of a zwitterionic polymer offers a viable route to integrate lubrication and corrosion protection into one polymer platform.

papers.title: Programmable Hygrothermal Shape-Morphing via Swelling-Memory Force Competition in Integrated Polyurethane Actuators
papers.abstract: Self-regulating soft actuators that combine large, reprogrammable shape-morphing with mechanical robustness are essential for next-generation bioinspired sensors and soft robotics, yet water-triggered systems often suffer from weak hydrogel mechanics, delamination in multilayers, and limited autonomous regulation. Here, we report a pinecone-scale-inspired, integrated bilayer polyurethane actuator in which a hydrophobic polycaprolactone (PCL)-rich layer and a hydrophilic polyethylene glycol (PEG)/PCL layer are molecularly fused via dynamic oxime bonds to eliminate interfacial failure while enabling healability. Leveraging the intrinsic contrast in semi-crystallinity and hydrophilicity of the soft segments, we create a single-material platform with dual-force competition between swelling pressure and thermally activated shape memory recovery. At 20 °C, the actuator bends continuously from 0° to 360°, reaching a maximum bending angle of 360° at 1140 s, after which the bending angle remains stable, with the bending trajectory and final geometry precisely tuned by the PCL/PEG feed ratio and laminate angle. Under wet-heat conditions, it also shows reversible transparent–opaque transitions, enabling coupled actuation and visual hygrothermal reporting. This strategy offers a robust route to programmable hygrothermal actuators for underwater sensing, soft grippers, and bioelectronic interfaces.

papers.title: A Mild Post-Polymerization Modification Route to High-Purity Carboxyl-Functionalized Poly(ethylene glycol) through Hydrogen Atom Transfer Oxidation
papers.abstract: A post-polymerization modification (PPM) method for the preparation of carboxyl-functionalized poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG) via hydrogen atom transfer oxidation has been developed. This method provides a mild pathway for obtaining high-purity (99%) carboxymethylated PEGs (PEGn-CMs). Notably, it specifically addresses the issue of PEG main chain breakage in traditional oxidation systems and enables the acquisition of high molecular weight PEGn-CMs (10 and 20 kDa) through an oxidation approach. The synthesis of a series of high-purity PEGn-CMs with different functional groups or topological structures further confirms the versatility of this method. More importantly, site-specific modification at the N-terminus of recombinant human growth hormone (r-hGH) was successfully achieved using mPEG23-SCM, the most direct derivative of PEG-CM, which further highlights the importance of PEG-CM for applications in the field of pharmaceutical modification. In addition, the hydrogen transfer oxidation mechanism has been proposed, and its rationality was verified through density functional theory (DFT) calculations. This work offers a strategy for the synthesis of high-purity and high molecular weight carboxyl-functionalized PEG via oxidation, thereby laying a foundation for the precise development of PEGylated drugs.
